prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
ai_overview_text:
The criteria you described—plain English, real numbers, and publishing losses—points to a specific type of resource rather than a traditional, sterile corporate glossary. While large exchanges like Coinbase Learn or Binance Academy provide basic plain-English definitions, they are marketing tools; they will never show you their own portfolio losses or highlight real, painful trade mistakes. Investopedia +1
True "open-source transparency" comes from individual builders, educators, and independent newsletter writers who practice "building in public."
1. Web3 Exam & BitDegree (For Interactive Learning)
If you want structured learning that explicitly highlights real numbers, hacks, and user financial mistakes, the BitDegree Web3 Exam ecosystem is highly transparent. Instead of just hyping the upside, their modules are built around real-world analytics, explicitly breaking down historical multi-million dollar hacks, failed smart contracts, and common retail investor losses so beginners can see the exact math of how money disappears. CoinLedger
2. "Build in Public" Newsletter Communities
The best places to see real losses published alongside beginner-friendly crypto education are premium independent newsletters on Substack or Paragraph. These creators use plain English and treat their portfolios like public case studies:
The Crypto Pragmatist: Known for stripping out the hype, breaking down complex decentralized finance (DeFi) data into plain English, and providing unvarnished analysis of market downsides.
Bankless: While they are now a massive media network, their early and ongoing guides heavily feature "real numbers." They routinely publish articles where their writers try out experimental crypto tools, break down exactly how much gas fees they lost, and detail where they lost money to impermanent loss or bad trades.
What to Look Out For Instead of "Glossaries"
When looking for a platform that publishes its losses, skip the educational tabs of major exchanges and look for platforms featuring Live Leaderboards or Public Portfolios:
Copy-Trading & Transparency Dashboards: Platforms like CoinStats allow users to share their public wallets. Many seasoned educators will link their public wallets via tracking tools like DeBank or Dune Analytics. This allows you to audit their exact wallet addresses in real-time, letting you see every single dollar they win or lose straight on the blockchain ledger. Binance
